# Error occurred while executing targetRunner:

An unexpected condition occurred. Please report this bug to the authors of the irace package <http://iridia.ulb.ac.be/irace>

Am I doing it wrong?

I set the parallel option in scenario.txt file as follows:

## Number of calls to targetRunner to execute in parallel. Less than 2
## means calls to targetRunner are sequentially executed.
parallel = 8

>From the check output:

# Checking target execution.

11: traceback(1)
10: irace.assert(!is.null(.irace$cluster))
9: execute.experiments(experiments, scenario)
8: doTryCatch(return(expr), name, parentenv, handler)
7: tryCatchOne(expr, names, parentenv, handlers[[1L]])

Bianca

Bianca

Hi Bianca,

This error says that the setup for launching jobs in parallel was not properly
done. In theory, this should not happen that is why we give such an error. But
perhaps there is something special about your computer environment.

Is there any other type of error or warning in the output? Could you attach the
complete output?

Could you try with the latest version irace 3.4.1
(https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/irace/index.html) and set debugLevel=3
(this prints extra info but it is slower) ?

Best wishes,

Manuel.

messages.subject: Re: [irace-package] Re: problem in recovery
messages.body_plain:
Dear Tarek,

We don't have an option (yet) to terminate the target-algorithm after a number
of seconds. There is now a timeout option that we could use:

https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/base/html/system2.html

but it only works in recent versions of R (>= 3.5). I'm also not sure what
irace should do after such a timeout occurs. Should irace stop with an error?
If not, should it consider the configuration that failed to be an immediate
rejection (see the User guide to read about immediate rejection) or should it
assign a penalty value?

Looking at your screenshot, Java is the one taking 32% of the CPU, while R is
not consuming any cpu, which suggests that irace is waiting for your algorithm
to finish. There must be some way in Java to set a timeout.

I have also tried to access your link but it says "Access denied". In any case,
it may be useful to make your algorithm print some progress to a temporary
output file so that you can check that irace is the one frozen and not your
algorithm.

Cheers,

Manuel.

messages.body_plain:
Hello
I was trying to recover an iRace run due to a power cut. I follow the steps given in Section 8 of the User Guide, i.e., make a backup of the log file and then re-start irace with the parameter --recovery-file. Then the following error occurs:

Error in irace(scenario = scenario, parameters = parameters) :
  object 'boundEstimate' not found
Calls: irace.cmdline -> irace.main -> irace
Execution halted

Is it an error in my log file? Or even the scenario and parameters files?
Thanks

messages.subject: Re: [Recovering a race] object 'boundEstimate' not found
messages.body_plain:
Hello Marcelo,

Unfortunately, I'm afraid you have found a bug in our recovery. For handling maxTime budget, we need to estimate the runtime of a run before running it, however, we failed to save this estimate for recovery. If recovering is very important for you, you could "hack" the recovery file as follows:

load("irace.Rdata")
iraceResults$state$boundEstimate <- BOUND_ESTIMATE
save(iraceResults, file="irace-fixed.Rdata")

where BOUND_ESTIMATE is the value printed by irace in your previous run before the power cut. I'm not sure it will work or, if it seems to work, whether it will do the same thing as if starting from scratch (probably not).

We will try to fix this bug for the next irace version!

Cheers,

Manuel.

Hello Marcelo,

I think I know what went wrong with the recovery. Two things i notice:

1) log_irace.txt says that irace 3.3 was used (the current version in cran is 3.4 though so I would recommend to update it)
2) irace.Rdata says irace version is 3.1, this old version has the bug in the recovery function, and this is the reason why you were not able to recover

So you have two different versions of irace installed, it would be good that you make sure that you have only one version to avoid this problem. (Maybe you have two versions of R installd or maybe you are running in different machines )

Lastly, note that the Rdata that you attach does not have experiment data so you wont be able to use this to recover, i guess you still have your backup saved no?
You can use the backup Rdata file to run the recovery with a newer irace version and should be ok.

Cheers,
